title: Upload general ledger accounts
path: /developer/v1/accounting/accounts
description: You can upload up to 500 general ledger accounts in an all-or-nothing fashion. If a general ledger accounts within a batch is malformed or violates a database constraint, the entire batch containing that account will be disregarded.
Accounts with matching external IDs on this connection are updated and reactivated if inactive. Accounts omitted from the upload are unchanged.
request: {
accounting_connection_id?: string | null
gl_accounts: {
classification: 'ANY' | 'ASSET' | 'CREDCARD' | 'EQUITY' | 'EXPENSE' | 'LIABILITY' | 'REVENUE' | 'UNKNOWN'
code?: string
entity_remote_ids?: string[]
id: string
name: string
}[]
}

accounting_connection_id?: string

code?: string
created_at: string /* date */
entity_remote_ids: string[] | null
gl_account_category_info?: {
id?: string
name?: string
ramp_id?: string
}
id?: string
is_active: boolean
name: string
provider_name: string | null
ramp_id: string
updated_at?: string /* date */
visibility?: 'HIDDEN' | 'VISIBLE'
}[]

}

}[]

target_field_remote_id: string
}[]
}
response: {

not_found_count: number
}

path: /developer/v1/accounting/field-option-filter-rules

Filterable by target_field_remote_id and target_field_option_remote_id.

target_field_remote_id: string
}[]
page: {
next: string | null
}
}
---
title: Bulk create field option filter rules
path: /developer/v1/accounting/field-option-filter-rules
description: Rules define which options of a target tracking category are available
based on selected options of trigger tracking categories.
Multiple rules for the same target option use OR logic between them.
Multiple required_selections within a single rule use AND logic.
request: {
accounting_connection_id?: string | null
rules: {
required_selections: {
trigger_field_option_remote_id: string
trigger_field_remote_id: string
}[]
target_field_option_remote_id: string
target_field_remote_id: string
}[]
}
response: {
created_count: number
duplicate_count: number
}

title: Upload new options
path: /developer/v1/accounting/field-options
description: You can upload up to 500 new field options for a given custom accounting field in an all-or-nothing fashion. If a field option within a batch is malformed or violates a database constraint, the entire batch containing that field option will be disregarded.
To have a successful upload, please sanitize the data and ensure the field options that you are trying to upload do not already exist on Ramp.
If a field option is already on Ramp but you want to update its attributes, please use the PATCH developer/v1/accounting/field-options/{id} endpoint instead.
request: {
accounting_connection_id?: string | null
field_id: string
options: {
code?: string
display_name?: string
entity_remote_ids?: string[]
id: string
value: string
}[]
}
response: {
accounting_connection_id: string
options?: {
accounting_connection_id: string
code?: string
created_at?: string /* date */
display_name?: string
entity_remote_ids: string[] | null
id?: string
is_active?: boolean
provider_name: string | null
ramp_id?: string
updated_at?: string /* date */
value?: string
visibility?: 'HIDDEN' | 'VISIBLE'
}[]
uploaded?: string[]
}

already exists on the bill.

title: Approve or reject a blank canvas workflow step
path: /developer/v1/blank-canvas-approvals/{approval_trigger_instance_id}
description: Blank canvas workflow steps require the `blank_canvas:write` scope. In a blank canvas workflow, external approval steps can be approved or rejected by the integration. Any other step is approved or rejected as an admin override, which requires the authorized user to have permission to manage workflow approvals (403 otherwise). For blank canvas workflow steps, repeating the action that already completed a step returns 200 without changes, and any other action on a step that is no longer pending returns 409.
The same endpoint decides the current external approval step of a transaction or reimbursement approval chain, which requires the `approvals:write` scope. Transaction steps support `approve` and `request_revision`, which requires a `reason`. Reimbursement steps support `approve` and `reject`, which requires a `reason`. A repeated or stale decision on a transaction or reimbursement step returns 409.
request: {
action: 'approve' | 'reject' | 'request_revision'
reason?: string | null
}
response: {
message: string
}

description: If a `reimbursement_id` is provided, the receipt will be linked directly to that reimbursement. If not, Ramp will attempt to automatically create a draft reimbursement via OCR.

---
title: Create a token
path: /developer/v1/token
description: Expects two headers:
- Authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`
- `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
Required content body depends on authorization type method, as defined by `grant_type`.
- Authorization Code Grant (`grant_type=authorization_code`): `grant_type`, `code`, and `redirect_uri` are required. Request must happen after requested scopes have been approved and exchanged for authorization code.
- Refresh Token Grant (`grant_type=refresh_token`): `grant_type` and `refresh_token` are required. User must have previously obtained refresh token in authorization code flow.
- Client Credentials Grant (`grant_type=client_credentials`): `grant_type` is required. If `scope` is omitted, the access token has no scopes.
- JWT Bearer Grant (`grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`): `grant_type` and an ID-JAG `assertion` are required. Issues a user-level access token without a refresh token.
request: {
assertion?: string
code?: string
grant_type: 'authorization_code' | 'client_credentials' | 'refresh_token' | 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer'
redirect_uri?: string
refresh_token?: string
scope?: string
}
response: {
access_token?: string
expires_in?: number
id_token?: string
refresh_token?: string
refresh_token_expires_in?: number | null
resource?: string | null
scope?: string
token_type?: string
}
---
title: Revoke an access or refresh token
path: /developer/v1/token/revoke
description: Expects an authorization header formed from base-64 encoded client credentials as `Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>`.
Content body must be form-encoded. Example:
```
curl \
-X POST \
-H "Authorization: Basic <base64-encoded client_id:client_secret>" \
-H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--data-urlencode 'token=$RAMP_API_TOKEN' \
'https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/token/revoke'
```
request: {
token: string
token_type_hint?: 'access_token' | 'refresh_token'
}
response: none

---
title: Create a procurement request
path: /developer/v1/unified-requests
description: Early access: enabled per business. Requires a business-scoped token.
Purchase-order and approval-only procurement spend programs are
supported; the request is created for `request_owner_id`. Pass
`submit: false` to create a draft without submitting it; otherwise, the
request is submitted into that program's approval flow by default. File-upload
form fields are not supported: a program whose form requires one cannot
be submitted through this endpoint, and the field is reported in
`additional_info.fields_to_answer`.
A vendor answer with `new_vendor_name` may include
`new_vendor_contact: {"email": "contact@example.com"}`. The contact is
saved as the new vendor's default before submission, including for drafts.
No separate contact field is needed on the program's form.
Set `request_blanket_purchase_order: true` to request a blanket PO, and
`is_total_amount_estimated` to mark the total as an estimate. Each is
rejected with `DEVELOPER_7195` when the program doesn't show its
question; `additional_info.validation_errors[].field_id` names the field.
Returns the request detail. Request-level selections appear under
`purchase_order.accounting_tracking_category_selections`
(`tracking_category.uuid` = `accounting_field_id`,
`tracking_category_option.uuid` = `accounting_field_option_id`). Lines
appear under `purchase_order.purchase_order_line_item_log_entries` with
their `id`, `accounting_tracking_category_selections`, and
`custom_field_values` (`column_id` = `custom_field_id`).

---
title: Edit a procurement request
path: /developer/v1/unified-requests/{unified_request_id}
description: Edits a native draft or submitted request as its owner. This action never
submits a draft; edits to a submitted request go through normal approval
reconciliation.
How each part of the body is applied:
- Top-level scalars (`name`, `currency`, `entity_id`, `start_date`,
`end_date`): omit to keep the saved value. `start_date` and `end_date`
accept `null` to clear.
- `request_blanket_purchase_order` and `is_total_amount_estimated`: omit to
keep the saved answer, `false` clears it. Each is rejected when the
spend program doesn't show its question for this request.
- `field_answers`: omit to keep all answers. When present, the list is the
complete set of API-editable answers: supported fields not listed are
cleared and `[]` clears them all. File-upload answers are never touched.
- `accounting_field_selections` (request level): omit to keep. When present,
the list is the complete set: enabled fields not listed are cleared and
`[]` clears all.
- `line_items`: omit to keep all lines. When present, the list is the
complete set of lines: a line with `id` is retained and updated, a line
without `id` is created, and any existing line whose `id` is not listed is
deleted. `[]` deletes every line (drafts only; a submitted request must
keep at least one line).
- Every line must carry `unit_price` and `unit_quantity`, and `description`
is written on every call: an omitted or `null` description clears it.
Always re-send `id` and `description` for lines you want to keep.
- A line's `accounting_field_selections` and `custom_field_values` follow
the collection rule: omit to keep the retained line's saved coding, send
the complete list to replace it (enabled fields not listed are cleared),
or send `[]` to clear it.
Returns the request detail. Request-level selections appear under
`purchase_order.accounting_tracking_category_selections`
(`tracking_category.uuid` = `accounting_field_id`,
`tracking_category_option.uuid` = `accounting_field_option_id`). Lines
appear under `purchase_order.purchase_order_line_item_log_entries` with
their `id`, `accounting_tracking_category_selections`, and
`custom_field_values` (`column_id` = `custom_field_id`).
X-Idempotency-Key is optional; reusing a key rejects the request rather
than replaying the original response.

---
title: Upload an attachment to a unified request
path: /developer/v1/unified-requests/{unified_request_id}/attachments
description: This endpoint accepts the [multipart/form-data](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/POST) format.
Include the file as a part named `file` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
Optionally include `attachment_type` as a form field with value `SPEND_REQUEST`
(default; supporting document on the request, not shared with the vendor) or
`PURCHASE_ORDER` (appended to the purchase order PDF sent to the vendor).
The request must also include an `X-Idempotency-Key` header.
request: {
attachment_type?: 'PURCHASE_ORDER' | 'SPEND_REQUEST'
file: string
}
response: {
id: string
}

title: Manage a user's invite lifecycle
path: /developer/v1/users/{user_id}/invite
description: Performs one of three actions against a draft user, delegating to the
Identity-owned invite / scheduled-invitation services:
- `SCHEDULE`: Create or update a scheduled invitation at `invitation_time`.
- `DESCHEDULE`: Cancel any pending scheduled invitation.
- `SEND_NOW`: Immediately publish the draft invite and send the invite email.
The user must be in DRAFT status for `SCHEDULE` and `SEND_NOW`.
`DESCHEDULE` is a no-op if no pending scheduled invitation exists.
request: {
action: 'DESCHEDULE' | 'SCHEDULE' | 'SEND_NOW'
invitation_time?: string /* date */
}
response: Record<string, unknown>
